summary:
Echoes in the Dust is an interactive web storytelling experience that brings NASA’s dormant robotic explorers on the Moon, Mars, and deep space back to life for school-age space enthusiasts. Instead of reading dense technical archives, learners explore 3D planetary surfaces, tune an analog radio dial across real mission frequencies, and establish simulated transmissions with six iconic spacecraft: Opportunity, InSight, Apollo 15 LRV, Surveyor 3, Voyager 1, and Cassini-Huygens.

Powered by grounded generative AI personas and optional voice synthesis, each spacecraft speaks in first person about its engineering, landing coordinates, and scientific discoveries—such as Opportunity’s hematite "blueberries" and InSight’s marsquake measurements—while adapting explanations for younger or older learners. By turning passive history into emotional, hands-on inquiry and gamified mission patches, Echoes in the Dust inspires the next generation to connect with the robotic pioneers that paved the way for modern space exploration.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

Echoes in the Dust addresses the "Abandoned but not Forgotten" challenge by transforming static archival data about retired and distant NASA spacecraft into an interactive, story-driven Mission Control experience. Explorers navigate a dark-mode telemetry interface featuring:

1. Interactive 3D Planetary Telemetry: Users inspect landing coordinates and mission profiles across the Moon, Mars, and deep space.

2. Analog Frequency Tuner: Using a procedural Web Audio API radio dial, learners sweep across MHz bands to clear static and lock onto the exact telemetry frequencies of six historic spacecraft: Opportunity (142.8 MHz), InSight Lander (138.4 MHz), Apollo 15 LRV (228.5 MHz), Surveyor 3 (216.2 MHz), Voyager 1 (8415.0 MHz), and Cassini-Huygens (8425.0 MHz).

3. Grounded AI Rover Personas & Voice Transmissions: Once connected, users hold live conversations with each spacecraft in first person. System prompts strictly ground every response in verified NASA mission records so the AI never fabricates historical events, while adapting scientific explanations to the learner's level. Users can also play synthesized voice transmissions to hear the spacecraft speak.

4. Mission Badges & Explorer Certificate: Reconnecting with all six explorers unlocks digital mission patches and generates a personalized downloadable Explorer Certificate.

Benefits & Intended Impact

Young learners often hear only about active missions while the decades of engineering behind historic landers, rovers, and probes remain hidden in dense technical documents. By giving these machines relatable personalities and connecting their physical instruments directly to the discoveries they unlocked, Echoes in the Dust fosters curiosity, emotional engagement, and accessible STEM learning in any browser with zero installation required.

Tools, Coding Languages & Software Used

- Frontend & Framework: Next.js (App Router), React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS

- 3D & Audio Visualization: Three.js / React Three Fiber, HTML5 Canvas, Web Audio API

- Super Intelligence (SI) & Voice Tools: Google Gemini API (for grounded first-person spacecraft dialogue) and ElevenLabs API (for optional voice synthesis), developed using VS Code and Google Antigravity

- Hosting & Version Control: GitHub and Vercel

Creativity & Design Considerations

We designed the interface around an atmospheric deep-space telemetry aesthetic—pairing tactile radio static, glowing orbital coordinates, and distinct spacecraft voices—while keeping accessibility central through zero-login browser access, responsive mobile layouts, and clear disclosures distinguishing verified NASA mission data from SI-generated dialogue and audio.
